questions.question: The Arabic word 'Islam' literally means
options: submission to the will of Allah
questions.explanation: Islam denotes submission, and a Muslim is one who submits to Allah.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The doctrine of Tawhid refers to
questions.explanation: Tawhid affirms the absolute unity of Allah and rejects associating partners with Him.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explanation: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The first pillar of Islam is
questions.explanation: The declaration of faith in the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: How many obligatory prayers must a Muslim observe each day?
questions.explanation: Subh, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Zakah refers to
options: the obligatory payment of alms on one's wealth
voluntary charity given at any time
the fast of the month of Ramadan
questions.explanation: Zakah is a fixed obligation on wealth above a minimum threshold.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Fasting during the month of Ramadan is known as
questions.explanation: Sawm is observed from dawn until sunset throughout Ramadan.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The pilgrimage to Makkah which every able Muslim should perform at least once is
questions.explanation: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those with the means and health.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Prophet Muhammad was born in
questions.explanation: He was born into the clan of Hashim of the tribe of Quraysh in Makkah.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Prophet Muhammad was born in about
questions.explanation: He was born around 570 CE, in what is remembered as the Year of the Elephant.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The father of the Prophet Muhammad was
questions.explanation: Abdullah died before the Prophet was born.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Prophet Muhammad's mother, who died when he was about six years old, was named
questions.explanation: Aminah died when the Prophet was about six years old.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: After the death of his grandfather, the Prophet Muhammad was brought up by his uncle
questions.explanation: Abu Talib took him into his household and later protected him in Makkah.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The first revelation came to the Prophet Muhammad in the cave of
questions.explanation: The cave of Hira is on the mountain of Nur near Makkah.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The angel who brought the revelation to the Prophet Muhammad was
questions.explanation: Jibril (Gabriel) is the angel entrusted with conveying revelation.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The first surah revealed to the Prophet Muhammad was
questions.explanation: Its opening command was 'Read, in the name of your Lord who created'.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The first wife of the Prophet Muhammad was
questions.explanation: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was the first to believe in his message.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The migration of the Prophet and his followers from Makkah to Madinah is called the
questions.explanation: The Hijrah marks the beginning of the Muslim community in Madinah.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Hijrah took place in
questions.explanation: The migration to Madinah occurred in 622 CE.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Islamic calendar is reckoned from
questions.explanation: Years are counted from the migration to Madinah and marked AH.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The first Caliph after the death of the Prophet Muhammad was
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq was chosen as the first successor.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The second Caliph of Islam was
questions.explanation: Under Umar the Muslim state expanded greatly and administration was organised.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Caliph during whose reign the text of the Qur'an was standardised into a single authorised copy was
questions.explanation: Uthman had standard copies prepared and distributed to the provinces.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The fourth of the Rightly Guided Caliphs was
questions.explanation: Ali was both cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali are collectively known as the
options: Imams of the schools of law
questions.explanation: They are the Khulafa' ar-Rashidun, who ruled immediately after the Prophet.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: How many surahs are there in the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an consists of 114 surahs of varying length.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The longest surah of the Qur'an is
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah, 'The Cow', is the longest chapter of the Qur'an.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The opening surah of the Qur'an is
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is recited in every unit of the obligatory prayers.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Surah Al-Ikhlas is principally concerned with
questions.explanation: It declares that Allah is One, eternal, and without offspring or equal.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Hadith refers to
options: the recorded sayings and deeds of the Prophet Muhammad
the text of the Qur'an itself
the ruling of a judge in a court
questions.explanation: Hadith reports what the Prophet said, did or approved.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Sunnah means
options: the practice and example of the Prophet
questions.explanation: The Sunnah is the model of conduct established by the Prophet.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The two primary sources of Islamic law are
options: the rulings of the four imams
questions.explanation: Ijma and Qiyas are secondary sources derived from these two.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Ijma as a source of Islamic law means
options: the consensus of qualified Muslim scholars
the direct command of the Qur'an
the personal opinion of a single scholar
the custom of the Arabs before Islam
questions.explanation: Where scholars agree on a ruling, that agreement carries authority.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Qiyas in Islamic jurisprudence refers to
options: reasoning by analogy from an established ruling
the abrogation of an earlier verse
the recitation of the Qur'an in public
questions.explanation: A new case is judged by analogy with a case already settled in the sources.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The ritual ablution performed with water before prayer is called
questions.explanation: Wudu involves washing the face, arms, head and feet in a prescribed order.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Tayammum is performed with
options: clean earth or sand when water is unavailable
questions.explanation: It is the permitted substitute for Wudu where water cannot be obtained or used.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Qiblah is the direction
questions.explanation: Muslims face the Ka'bah when performing the prayers.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The call to prayer in Islam is known as
questions.explanation: The Adhan summons the faithful; the Iqamah announces that prayer is beginning.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The congregational prayer observed on Fridays is called
questions.explanation: It is preceded by a sermon, the Khutbah, delivered by the Imam.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The festival that marks the end of the fast of Ramadan is
questions.explanation: Id al-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The festival of sacrifice, observed during the period of pilgrimage, is
questions.explanation: It commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The night journey of the Prophet from Makkah to Jerusalem and his ascension are known as
questions.explanation: The five daily prayers are traditionally associated with this event.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Battle of Badr was fought in
questions.explanation: It took place in 2 AH, corresponding to 624 CE, and ended in victory for the Muslims.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The conquest of Makkah by the Muslims took place in
questions.explanation: Makkah was entered peacefully in 8 AH, about 630 CE.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Prophet Muhammad died in
questions.explanation: He died in 11 AH, corresponding to 632 CE.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Prophet Muhammad died and was buried in
questions.explanation: His grave is in Madinah, within the precinct of the Prophet's Mosque.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: Twenty-five prophets are named, although many more were sent.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The Islamic belief in the life to come is known as
questions.explanation: Akhirah is belief in resurrection, judgement and the hereafter.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: The jihad of Usman dan Fodio, which led to the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate, began in
questions.explanation: The jihad began in 1804 and reshaped the political order of Hausaland.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies

questions.question: Islam first reached the Kanem-Borno area of Nigeria mainly through
questions.explanation: Traders and scholars crossing the Sahara brought the faith from North Africa.
questions.subject: Islamic Studies
